dedupe_keys.name: mexico city water crisis 2024 drought cutzamala system water losses and integrity failures water integrity network

description: This case study is a Water Integrity Network long-read on the 2024 water crisis in Greater Mexico City, home to nearly 23 million people, when 84 percent of Mexico was in some degree of drought and all of Mexico City in severe drought as of 15 May 2024, raising fears of a Day Zero. It argues that lack of water is not the only cause: rapid growth and loss of green areas reduce aquifer recharge, permits are said to be granted indiscriminately or illegally, and abstraction controls are weak even where wells are permitted. The city depends on aquifers hundreds of metres deep and on water from more than 100 kilometres away through the Cutzamala reservoir system; over-extraction is making the city sink, and water losses reach about 40 percent from deteriorating pipes and illegal connections. Coverage: one metropolitan area and one drought, an advocacy analysis with headline figures. Access: free web article; licence not stated. Caveats: an opinion piece with claims that are cited to press, not primary data. It informs urban water supply drought, non-revenue water and groundwater overdraft scenarios, and lists no linked catalogue records.
